'''R6-D8''' was an [[R6 astromech droid]]<ref name="By the Numbers" /> that served in the [[Resistance]] as the [[Astromech droid|astromech]] of [[Temmin Wexley]].<ref name="Poe Dameron: Flight Log" /> He<ref name="TROS VD" /> [[Death|perished]] alongside his master when their [[Temmin Wexley's X-wing|T-70 X-wing starfighter]] was downed into a [[Star Destroyer]] by the [[Sith Eternal military|Sith Eternal forces]] during the [[Battle of Exegol]], [[Time|moments]] before the arrival of the [[Citizens' Fleet]].<ref name="TROS" />

Before his death, R6-D8 learned of [[Mister Bones]], Wexley's late reprogrammed [[B1-series battle droid]], after studying his masters logs. Seeking to please Wexley, R6-D8 tried to make himself more aggressive. However, he did not dare to overwrite the factory-set safety inhibitors in his personality matrix.<ref name="TROS VD" />

{{Droid-stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
R6-D8 first appeared in [[Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens|''Star Wars'': Episode VII ''The Force Awakens'']],<ref name="TFA" /> albeit unnamed. He was first identified in the [[2016]] reference book ''[[Poe Dameron: Flight Log]]''.<ref name="Poe Dameron: Flight Log" />

In the non-[[canon]]ical game ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Force Awakens]]'', Snap Wexley's astromech malfunctions, requiring him to rebuild a new one. The three options for Snap to rebuild are [[R2-D3]], [[R4-P44]], and [[Q7-series astromech droid|Q7]]. However, the malfunctioning astromech is not identified as R6-D8.<ref name="LSWTFA">''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Force Awakens]]''</ref> The Lego Star Wars set "Resistance X-Wing Fighter" features Snap Wexley's X-Wing, however it does not have R6-D8, nor any astromech for that matter.<ref name="Resistance X-Wing">{{LEGOCite|type=micro|num=75125|name=Resistance X-wing Fighter}}</ref>
